legend: Highly cellular tumour with neuroblasts seen singly and in tissue fragments admixed with neuropil, and occasionally in pseudorosettes. The neuroblasts have scant, indistinct cytoplasm and round, ovoid, or angulated, mildly pleomorphic nuclei (Giemsa).

Dispersed neuroblasts with round, ovoid, angular, or irregular nuclei and scant cytoplasm, admixed with larger cells with scant or more abundant eccentric cytoplasm, suggesting early ganglionic differentiation; however, recognizable ganglion cells are not present, and neuropil is absent. Small lymphocytes are present in the background (Giemsa).

Neuroblasts within this fragment of fibrillar neuropil have indistinct cytoplasmic borders and round, oval, or angulated nuclei with finely granular chromatin. Single neuroblasts are present in the background (Giemsa).

Pleomorphic cells including neuroblasts with scant cytoplasm admixed with larger cells showing ganglionic differentiation in the form of abundant, eccentric cytoplasm and enlarged, round nuclei; binucleate forms are present. Delicate fibrillar matrix is present in the background (Giemsa).

Sheets of neuroblasts admixed with variable amounts of neuropil. The cells in this field are relatively uniform, with scant cytoplasm and round, ovoid, or angulated nuclei with fine chromatin. Pseudorosettes are evident. Cells with ganglionic differentiation are absent. A few mitotic figures and karyorrhectic cells are present (cell block, H&E).
